newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks rise as Fed meets.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks rise as Fed meets.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks rose Tuesday as Wall Street awaited President Clinton's State of the Union address and the conclusion Wednesday of the Federal Reserve's policy-setting meeting.
The Dow Jones industrial average, which was off most of the session, rebounded in the last half hour to close 27.32 points higher at 6,833.48.
In the broader market, however, declining issues led advances 1,263 to 1,163 on active volume of 491 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Investors displayed a cautious demeanor, as they awaited the outcome of the Federal Open Market Committee's two-day meeting, which started Tuesday, to set the course for interest rates.
The Fed has held interest rates steady for more than a year, since cutting them by a quarter percentage point on Jan. 31, 1996.

With the Fed meeting underway and President Clinton scheduled to deliver his State of the Union speech Tuesday night, stocks extended a hiatus from the volatility they displayed during most of January.
"Things really do seem to be in a holding pattern," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.
In the bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury rose 13/32, lowering its yield to 6.71 percent from 6.74 percent on Monday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
While most sectors saw little action, there were pockets of activity. Technology stocks weakened on speculation about growth prospects in the networking industry.
"The networkers have been under pressure," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management. "Generally speaking there's a lot of nervousness in the group."

The Nasdaq market's most active list was peppered with networking names that fell victim to the jittery selling. Xylan Corp. tumbled 6-1/2 to 22 after reporting earnings that were just shy of estimates.
3Com Corp. sank 3-3/4 to 58-3/4, extending a slide that has taken the stock down about 20 percent over the last two weeks.
The selling pressure spread to networking bellwether Cisco Systems Inc., which reported earnings after the close of trading.

Cisco said it earned 49 cents a share in the latest quarter, up from 31 cents a year ago but the earnings were still one cent a share below Wall Street's estimate. The stock, which fell 1-1/8 to 67-1/8 in the regular market hours, lost more ground in after hours trading, dropping to 65.

Financial stocks were generally strong, with Chase Manhattan Corp. up 2-5/8 to 96-3/8 and BankAmerica Corp. rising 1-3/8 to 114-5/8. Analysts said sector took its cue from a drop in the Treasury's bond yields.

"The bond market appears to be confident about the possibility of a balanced budget amendment," Ackerman said. "The market will be listening carefully tonight during the State of the Union for signals about progress in balancing the budget," he said.
During the day, leading Republicans expressed optimism that a balanced budget amendment would win passage in both the House of Representatives and Senate.
Among other individual issues, Olympic Financial Ltd. fell two to 12-5/8 after Oppenheimer & Co. downgraded its opinion of the stock.

PaineWebber Group Inc. rose 3-1/8 to 38-7/8. The company declined to comment as a matter of policy after the NYSE requested a statement regarding the unusual activity in its shares. The firm has been the subject of takeover speculation in recent weeks.
The Nasdaq Composite index fell 2.30 points to 1,373.75.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 2.53 to 789.26. The American Stock Exchange index slipped 0.46 to 589.25.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 0.86 to 413.34. The average share was up 9 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,592.64, up 5.885 or 0.08 percent.
